newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TWO FIVE NATIONS' MATCHES TO BE PLAYED ON SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TWO FIVE NATIONS' MATCHES TO BE PLAYED ON SUNDAY.

text.p: Two of next year's Five Nations' championship matches, including the Calcutta Cup clash between England and Scotland, will be played on Sunday.
After the Calcutta Cup match at Murrayfield on Sunday March 22, Wales will meet France at Wembley on Sunday April 5.
Starting times of Saturday matches will be staggered in a bid to attract a wider audience.
"We believe that playing some of the matches on Sundays will be an exciting new concept that will enhance the tournament," Five Nations chief executive Roger Pickering said on Friday.
"It is the express wish of the Five Nations' committee to enable as big an audience as possible to witness the oldest and most respected rugby tournament in the world.
"By staggering the kick-off times on a Saturday and spreading some rounds of the championship over two days, the game will be able to massively broaden its appeal.
February 7 - France v England (kick-off time to be announced)
